The Directorate strengthens the quality of

education in private schools by providing

continuous professional development

opportunities for teachers. Capacity-building

programmes focus on effective curriculum

implementation, innovative pedagogical practices

and adoption of the revised curriculum, thereby

improving classroom transactions and student

learning outcomes.

enabling teachers to effectively implement the

revised curriculum and improve classroom

practices.

6.6 Conclusion

The Directorate of Private Schools continues

to strengthen the regulation and development of

private school education through transparent

governance, student-centred interventions,

academic support and continuous teacher

professional development. By ensuring equitable

access to education, promoting safe learning

environments, strengthening statutory

compliance and delivering efficient regulatory

services through technology-enabled systems.

94

well-regulated, accountable and quality-oriented

private school education system that

complements Tamil Nadu's vision of inclusive,

equitable and high-quality school education.

The Directorate of Government

Examinations (DGE) is the State's examination

authority responsible for conducting public

examinations, scholarship examinations and other

statutory examinations, ensuring fairness,

transparency and integrity in the assessment

administering large-scale examinations,

evaluating student performance, issuing

certificates and implementing examination

reforms that facilitate academic progression and

lifelong learning.

7.2 Public Examinations and Academic Progression

The Directorate conducts public and

statutory examinations that facilitate academic

progression, certification and lifelong learning.

The White Paper on fiscal management of Tamil Nadu that was published in June 2026 sets the roadmap for better revenue mobilisation and administrative reforms, and has inter alia observed that the decline across major taxes like GST, VAT, and excise including revenues from mines and minerals has been mainly driven by administrative choices, leakages and corruption in the past rather than an underlying economic slowdown. It has also indicated that resolving this shortfall requires long-term, multi-year reforms focused on curbing corruption, enforcing compliance, and mobilizing resources efficiently. Some of the key factors highlighted in the White Paper are outlined below:

e Own-tax effort at a historic low — the SOTR-to-GSDP ratio fell to 5.45% in 2025-26, the lowest in two decades showing the sharpest decline among peer States in recent years.

e Large revenue foregone — decline in SOTR amounts to about Rs.1.23 lakh crore of annual revenue foregone, roughly 90% of the fiscal deficit in 2025-26.

e Unique to Tamil Nadu — Peer States like Maharashtra, and Karnataka have held on or have shown growth in SoTR-GSDP ratio, while Tamil Nadu alone has registered a steady decline.

e Broad-based weakness — the fall is reflected in all major taxes: GST, VAT on petroleum, State Excise, Stamp Duty and Motor Vehicle Tax.

e Cause is administrative, not structural — attributed to leakages, systemic corruption and administrative choices, primarily in commercial taxes, registration, excise and mining.

1.Preparation and enforcement of land use planning and zoning regulations incorporating infrastructure and

hazard restrictions.

It is proposed that formal land use planning and zoning regulations shall mandatorily incorporate critical parameters such as the availability of trunk infrastructure, including water supply, electricity, and sanitation systems, to ensure that development is aligned with service capabilities. Further, hazard mapping shall form an integral component of planning, identifying areas where development is prohibited due to natural hazards. In addition, hazard maps_ shall specify minimum separation between residential zones and hazardous occupancies. Accordingly, it is proposed to mandate the preparation and enforcement of land use plans and zoning regulations incorporating mandatory infrastructure requirements

and hazard-based restrictions.

2.Hazard maps shall be formally approved and published with prohibited zones, separation distances, no

construction areas

awareness and implementation.

-3-

3.Establishing a regulatory framework to define zoning parameters based on availability of trunk infrastructure

There is a need to establishing a regulatory framework that defines zoning parameters based on the availability and adequacy of trunk infrastructure. This framework shall ensure that development permissions are granted only where infrastructure systems are sufficient or planned to meet the projected demand, thereby preventing overburdening of services and ensuring orderly growth.

4. The above proposed measures are expected to result in a scientifically robust and legally enforceable planning system that promotes sustainable development, enhances public safety, protects natural resources, and ensures efficient utilization of infrastructure. It will also improve transparency, strengthen governance, and support informed decision-making.

5. In view of the above, the Commissioner of Town and Country Planning has requested the Government. issue necessary orders mandating the integration of infrastructure availability and hazard considerations into land use planning and zoning regulations, approving -and publishing hazard maps indicating prohibited zones, separation distances, and no-construction areas, and establishing a- regulatory framework to define zoning parameters based on the availability of trunk infrastructure.

6. After careful consideration, the Government hereby, accept the request of Commissioner of Town and Country Planning and issue orders for mandating the integration of infrastructure availability and hazard considerations into land use planning and zoning regulations, approving and publishing hazard maps indicating prohibited zones, separation distances, and. no-construction areas, and establishing a regulatory framework to define zoning parameters based on the availability of trunk infrastructure.

9.7. Government Silk Reeling / Twisting Units

Government Multi-end silk Reeling Units are functioning as model units for reeling and twisting entrepreneurs, in order to support the post cocoon sector which is vital for sericulture industry.

There are 9 Government Reeling Units functioning under this department. Production capacity of these Silk reeling units is 27 Metric Tonnes per annum. Of these 9 silk reeling units, Hosur, Salem, Talavady and Nannagaram are functioning as Silk Reeling cum Twisting Units, where the raw silk is further converted as twisted silk (or ready silk).

9.8. Government Anna Silk Exchange, Kancheepuram

The raw silk produced by silk reelers in the State is transacted through the Government Anna Silk Exchanges functioning at Kancheepuram and Salem. The exchange has been functioning since 1991. The Government Anna Silk Exchanges serve as regulated markets, providing silk reelers

29

with an organised platform for marketing their raw silk.

Based on the quality assessment of silk and the prevailing average cocoon price of the state, floor price is fixed and silk lots are admitted for auction. Master weavers, Twisters and the TANSILK representatives participate in the open auction and purchase the silk. 0.75% of silk transaction value is collected as levy each from seller and buyer.

During the year 2025-2026, 110.302 Metric Tonnes of Raw Silk has been transacted for a value of Rs.5,629.570 lakh in Anna Silk Exchange, Kancheepuram and its Salem branch.

The Tamil Nadu Cooperative Silk Producers' Federation (TANSILK) was registered in 1978 and is functioning as the apex cooperative federation of the silk cooperative societies in Tamil Nadu at Kancheepuram with the objective of safeguarding the interests of sericulture farmers, silk reelers, silk twisters, weavers, and Sarvodaya Sanghs by

ORDER: -

The Hon'ble Minister for Finance, Planning and Development has made the following announcement among others on the floor of Assembly on 05.08.2026: -

"A Comprehensive Human-Wildlife-Conflict Mitigation Scheme will be introduced, incorporating scientific measures such as hanging solar fences and steel wire rope fencing, community-based protection of forests, appointment of forest protection staff, and GPS-enabled vehicles for conflict management, night patrolling, security and monitoring across 100 conflict-prone villages in Coimbatore, Dharmapuri, Dindigul, Erode, Krishnagiri, The Nilgiris, Salem, Theni, Tirunelveli, Tenkasi and Tiruppur districts. An amount of Rs.20.00 crore has been allocated for this in the current financial year."

2. In the letter second read above, the Principal Chief Conservator of Forests and Chief Wildlife Warden has sent a detailed proposal seeking Administrative Sanction for an amount of Rs.180.00 crore for implementation of the "Comprehensive Human-Wildlife Conflict Mitigation Scheme" in Tamil Nadu for a period of five years from 2026-2027 to 2030-2031.The scheme is proposed to be implemented for a period of five years from

2

2026-2027 to 2030-2031. The principal interventions proposed under the scheme include:-

(i). Provision of hanging solar fences at vulnerable locations; (ii). Provision of steel wire rope fencing and other suitable physical barriers; (iii). Community-based protection of forests and participation of local communities in conflict mitigation: (iv). Deployment of forest protection staff in vulnerable areas; (v). Provision of GPS-enabled vehicles for conflict management, patrolling and rapid response; (vi). Strengthening of night patrolling, security and surveillance: (vii). Monitoring of wildlife movement in conflict-prone areas: and (viii). Other allied measures required for effective mitigation of human-wildlife conflict.
